newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee ends up vs dollar due to no demand.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee ends up vs dollar due to no demand.

text.p: COLOMBO, Dec 13 - The Sri Lanka rupee closed stronger on Friday due to lack of significant corporate demand for dollars ahead of the holiday season, dealers said.

The rupee closed at 56.76 to the U.S. currency after opening at 56.80. The central bank reacted to the dollar's strengthening overseas by pushing it up by 1.5 local cents. It fixed buying at 56.0761 and selling at 57.2009.
"The dollar picked up due to the range, but did not manage to go far," a Standard Chartered Bank dealer said.
"There was no real demand (for the dollar). There is also a lack of corporate demand just ahead of holidays," she said.
Other dealers said some foreign banks vied for forwards in the market late in the day.
"Some activity was seen in the forward market, may be for speculative purposes," a Commercial Bank dealer said.
Overnight call money closed at 14 percent.

"Though call rates are down, banks feel its not good enough for them to build up on exchange positions. They feel it is too late in the year for any depreciation to take place," the Standard Chartered dealer said.
